name: signatures
headline: One address: the *signature*
say: Everything in Hypercomb has one kind of address: a signature, a fingerprint computed from the content itself. The same content gets the same signature, on every machine, in every country, for good. Change one byte, and it is a different thing, with a different signature. So the signature proves the content. The same picture, kept twice, is kept once. And a signature can be passed along as a short string that anyone can check. It does not ask you to trust a company. It lets you check for yourself.
